Name of the Surah

• It is called Ar-Ra'd (The Thunder), because the mention of thunder occurs in it, and it is not mentioned in any earlier Meccan surah in terms of the order of revelation.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Affirming God Most High's sole divinity, through evidence of the creation of the upper world and the lower world and their order, which indicate that He - glory be to Him - alone possesses perfect knowledge and power, and clarifying a number of the manifestations of divine power, and that whatever is other than God among the alleged deities possesses neither harm nor benefit.

• Refuting the claims and assertions of the polytheists in denying the Resurrection, and warning them that what befell those like them among the deniers will befall them.

• Mentioning the attributes of the people of felicity and the people of wretchedness through the use of parables in clarifying their conditions, and clarifying the final outcome of each of the two groups in the Hereafter.

• Clarifying the stance of the disbelievers toward the Qur'an and the revelation and their denial of the Message, and their obstinacy in demanding that signs come in the manner they wish, contrasted with the certainty of the believers, and that what the Messenger (ﷺ) encountered from his people is of the same kind as what the messengers (peace be upon them) before him encountered.

[The Exegesis]

﴿Alif Lam Mim Ra.﴾ The discussion of the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah) has already preceded at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah. These are the verses of the Qur'an, of exalted rank, and this Qur'an revealed to you - O Messenger - is the truth, not as the polytheists say: that you bring it from your own self. Yet, despite this, most people do not believe in it nor act upon it.

Allah, exalted is He, is the One who raised the seven heavens by His power without pillars that you can see, then He istawa (that is, He rose above and ascended) over the Throne in a manner befitting His majesty and greatness. He subjected the sun and the moon for the benefit of the servants; each of them runs in its orbit (falak) until the Day of Resurrection. He, glorified is He, manages the affairs of this world and the Hereafter, and He makes clear to you the signs (ayat) that indicate His power and that there is no god except Him, so that you may be certain of Allah and of your return to Him, and thus believe in His promise and His warning, and devote worship to Him alone.

He is the One who spread out the earth, making it wide and extended, and prepared it for your living. He placed in it mountains to hold it firm, and rivers for your drinking and your benefit. And He made in it two kinds of every fruit: some were white and some black, some sweet and some sour. And He made the night cover the day with its darkness. Indeed, in all of that are lessons for a people who reflect upon them, so that they take heed.

And on the earth are neighboring tracts, some fertile, producing what benefits people, and some saline and brackish, producing nothing. There are gardens of grapevines, fields of varied crops, and palm trees, some growing in clusters from a single root and some growing separately. All of this is in one soil and is watered with one water, yet they differ in their fruits, their sizes, their tastes and other qualities: this one is sweet and that one is sour, and some are better than others for eating. Indeed, in that are signs for people who have hearts that understand from Allah, the Exalted, His command and His prohibition.

If you, O Messenger, are amazed at the disbelief of the disbelievers after these proofs, then more amazing still is their saying: "When we have died and become dust, will we indeed be resurrected anew?" Those are the ones who deny their Lord, who brought them into being from nothingness. Those are the ones for whom there will be chains of fire around their necks on the Day of Resurrection, and those are the ones who will enter the Fire, remaining in it forever, never to emerge from it.

The disbelievers ask you to hasten the punishment, before the good health of faith that brings security and good deeds, though I have not hastened it upon them before. Indeed, the punishments of the disbelievers before them have already passed, so how is it that they do not take warning from them? Indeed your Lord, O Messenger, is certainly Possessor of forgiveness for the sins of those who repent of their sins among mankind despite their wrongdoing. He opens for them the door of forgiveness and calls them to it, while they wrong themselves through their disobedience to their Lord. And indeed your Lord is severe in punishment toward those who persist in disbelief, misguidance, and disobedience to Allah.

The disbelievers of Makkah say: "Why was he not given a tangible miracle, like the staff of Musa and the she-camel of Salih?" But that is not in your hand, O Messenger; you are only a conveyer of the message to them, and a warner of them against the punishment of Allah. And every nation has had a messenger who guides them to Allah, the Exalted.

Allah, the Exalted, knows what every female carries in her womb: whether it is male or female, and whether it will be wretched or happy. He knows what the wombs lose, so that the fetus miscarries or is born before nine months, and what their pregnancy adds to them. Everything is decreed by Allah in a specific measure of decrease or increase, and it does not exceed that measure.

Allah knows what is hidden from the eyes and what is witnessed. He is the Great in His essence, names, and attributes, and the Exalted above all His creation in His essence, His power, and His dominance.

It is equal to His knowledge whether one of you conceals his speech or speaks it aloud, and it is equal to Him whether one hides his deeds in the darkness of the night or displays them in the brightness of the day.

God has angels who follow one another in succession over the human being, from before him and from behind him. They guard him by the command of God, and they record whatever proceeds from him of good or evil. Indeed, God, glorified and exalted is He, does not change a blessing He has bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves by disobeying Him. And if God wills a trial for a people, there is no escaping it, and they have no guardian besides God who would take charge of their affairs, bringing them what they love and warding off what they dislike.

He it is who shows you lightning as one of His signs, [the bright light that flashes through the clouds], so that you fear it may bring down upon you destructive thunderbolts, and you hope that rain will come with it. By His power, the Exalted, He brings into being the clouds heavy with abundant water for your benefit.

And the thunder glorifies God with His praise, a glorification that shows its submission to its Lord, and the angels exalt their Lord out of their fear of God. God sends the destroying thunderbolts, and with them He destroys whomever He wills of His creatures, while the disbelievers dispute about God's oneness and His power to resurrect. He is mighty in strength, power, and seizing those who disobey Him.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 13, verse 14:

To Allah, glorified and exalted, alone belongs the call to monotheism, "There is no god but Allah." Thus none is worshipped or called upon except Him. As for the deities they worship besides Allah, they do not answer the supplication of those who call upon them. Their situation with them is like that of a thirsty person who stretches out his palms toward water from afar, so that it might reach his mouth, yet it never reaches it. The supplication of the disbelievers to them is nothing but utmost error from the truth, because they associate others with Allah.

To Allah alone prostrate, in submission and obedience, all who are in the heavens and the earth. The believers prostrate and submit to Him willingly and by choice, while the disbelievers submit to Him against their will, because they are arrogant toward worshipping Him, while their own condition and their innate nature (fitrah) contradict them in that, and the shadows of created things yield to the greatness of Allah, moving by His will at the beginning of the day and at its end.

Say, [O Messenger], to the polytheists: "Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?" Say: "Allah." Say: "Is it that you have taken, besides Him, protectors who do not control benefit or harm for themselves?" Then say to them, binding them with proof: Have you taken besides Him gods worshipped by you, while they cannot benefit or harm themselves, let alone benefit or harm you, and you have abandoned worshipping their Owner? Say to them, [O Messenger]: Are the disbeliever, who is like the blind, and the believer, who is like the seeing, equal in your view? Or are disbelief, which is like darkness, and faith, which is like light, equal in your view? Or have their protectors whom they have made partners with Allah created the like of His creation, so that the creation of the partners became confused with the creation of Allah, and so they believed that they deserved worship? Say to them, [O Messenger]: Allah, exalted is He, is the Creator of every existing thing from non-existence, and He alone deserves to be worshipped; He is the One, the Subduer, who alone deserves divinity and worship, not the idols and images that neither harm nor benefit.

Then Allah, glorified is He, struck a parable for truth and falsehood with water that He sent down from the sky. So the valleys of the earth flowed with it according to their capacity, large and small, and the torrent carried a foam that rose and floated on its surface, having no benefit in it. He struck another parable: it is that of metals, over which people kindle fire to smelt them, seeking adornment, as with gold and silver, or seeking benefits from which they profit, as with copper. Its dross then comes out, having no benefit in it, like that which was with the water. In this same way Allah strikes the parable of truth and falsehood: falsehood is like the foam of the water and the dross of the metals, which vanishes or is cast away, since it has no benefit; while truth is like the clear water, and the pure metals, which remain in the earth for people to benefit from. As He has explained these parables to you, so He strikes them for mankind, in order that truth may be made clear from falsehood, and guidance from error.

For the believers who obeyed Allah and His Messenger is Paradise. As for those who did not obey and disbelieved in Him, theirs is the Fire. Even if they possessed everything on earth and the like of it along with it, they would offer it as ransom to save themselves from the punishment of Allah on the Day of Resurrection, and it would not be accepted from them. Those will be called to account for every evil deed they committed before, and their abode and dwelling place is Hell, which will be a bed for them. What a wretched bed it is that they have prepared for themselves.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 13, verses 19–20:

Is the one who knows that what has come down to you, O Messenger, from Allah is the truth, and so believes in it, like the one who is blind to the truth and does not believe? Only people of sound minds take heed, those who fulfill the covenant of Allah that He has commanded them, and do not break the solemn pact they made with Allah.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 13, verses 19–20:

Is the one who knows that what has come down to you, O Messenger, from Allah is the truth, and so believes in it, like the one who is blind to the truth and does not believe? Only people of sound minds take heed, those who fulfill the covenant of Allah that He has commanded them, and do not break the solemn pact they made with Allah.

They are the ones who maintain the ties Allah has commanded to be maintained, such as ties of kinship and care for the needy. They are mindful of their Lord, and they fear that He will call them to account for all their sins, and that He will not forgive any of them.

This is the commentary on Qur'an 13:22 from the King Fahd Complex's al-Tafsir al-Muyassar.

Those are the ones who were patient in the face of harm and in obedience, and in abstaining from disobedience, seeking the pleasure of their Lord. They performed the prayer in its most complete forms, and paid from their wealth their obligatory zakat, and voluntary spending, both in secret and in public. They repel evil with good, so it erases it. Those described with these qualities have the praiseworthy outcome in the Hereafter.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 13, verse 23:

That final outcome is the Gardens of Eden (Jannat ʿAdn), where they will dwell forever and never leave them. With them will be the righteous among their fathers, their wives, and their offspring, both males and females. The angels will enter upon them from every gate to congratulate them on their entry into Paradise.

**Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 13, verse 24:**

The angels say to them: "Peace be upon you," a special greeting of honor for you. You have been saved from every evil because of your patience in obeying Allah. "How excellent is the final abode: Paradise."

As for the wretched, they have been described with the opposite of the attributes of the believers. They are those who do not fulfil the covenant of Allah, which is to single Him out, glorified be He, in worship after they had affirmed it upon themselves, and they are those who sever what Allah has commanded to be joined, such as the ties of kinship and other things, and they cause corruption on the earth by committing acts of disobedience. Those who are described with these ugly attributes have for themselves expulsion from the mercy of Allah, and for them is what will distress them of severe punishment in the Hereafter.

God alone expands provision for whomever He wills of His servants, and restricts it for whomever He wills among them. The disbelievers rejoiced in the abundance of worldly life, yet the life of this world, compared with the Hereafter, is nothing but a little enjoyment that quickly passes away.

The disbelievers say, out of obstinacy: "Why was a tangible miracle not sent down upon Muhammad, like the miracle of Musa and Isa?" Say to them: Indeed, Allah leads astray whomever He wills of the stubborn ones from guidance, and miracles do not benefit them; and He guides to His true religion whoever turns back to Him and seeks His good pleasure.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 13, verse 28:

And [Allah] guides those whose hearts find rest in the Oneness of Allah and His remembrance, so their hearts are at peace. Indeed, it is by obedience to Allah, by remembering Him, and by [hoping for] His reward that hearts are made tranquil and find comfort.
Those who believed in Allah and His Messenger and did righteous deeds will have joy and delight of the eye, a good state, and a good return to the Paradise of Allah and His pleasure.

As We sent the messengers before you, so We have sent you, [O Messenger], to a community before which other communities have passed away, so that you may recite to them the Qur'an revealed to you, while your people disbelieve in the Oneness of the Most Merciful. Say to them, [O Messenger]: The Most Merciful, whom you have not taken as a single God, is my Lord; there is no deity worthy of worship except Him. In Him I have placed my reliance and trust, and to Him is my return and turning back.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 13, verse 31:

God responds to the disbelievers who demanded that tangible miracles be sent down upon the Prophet ﷺ, saying to them: Even if there were a Qur'an by which mountains would be moved from their places, or the earth would be split open into rivers, or by which the dead would be brought to life and made to speak, as you have demanded of you, [this Qur'an] would be the one characterized by that, not anything else, and yet they would not believe in it. Rather, to God alone belongs the entire matter concerning miracles and other things. Have not the believers known that if God willed, all the people of the earth would have believed without any miracle? The disbelievers will continue to be struck by a calamity because of their disbelief, such as killing and captivity in the battles of the Muslims, or that calamity will descend near their dwellings, until the promise of God comes, [which is] victory over them. Indeed, God does not break His promise.

And if they have mocked your message, O Messenger, then nations before you also mocked their messengers. So do not grieve, for I granted respite to those who disbelieved, then I seized them with My punishment, and My punishment was severe.

Is then He who stands over every soul, watching over what it earns, (to be worshipped as equal to those who have no power)? Yet they have assigned partners to God from among His creation. Say, [O Messenger]: Name them, and describe them. Or are you informing God of partners on earth that He does not know? Or is it mere outward words, with no reality behind them? Rather, Satan has made their false statement appealing to the disbelievers and has barred them from the way of God. And whomever God does not guide, no one can guide.

For these disbelievers who bar others from the way of Allah, there is a harsh punishment in the life of this world, through killing, captivity, and disgrace. Their punishment in the Hereafter is even more severe and intense. They have no one to shield them from the punishment of Allah.

The description of the Garden that Allah has promised to those who fear Him: rivers flow beneath its trees and its palaces. Its fruit never ends and its shade never passes away or diminishes. That is the reward of the Garden, the final outcome of those who feared Allah, so they avoided His prohibitions and performed His obligations; and the final outcome of the disbelievers in Allah is the Fire.

Those to whom We gave the Scripture, from among the Jews and the Christians, among them those who believed in you, such as ʿAbdullah ibn Salam and al-Najashi, rejoice at the Qur'an revealed to you, because it agrees with what they have. And among the factions that band together in disbelief against you, such as al-Sayyid and al-ʿAqib, the two bishops of Najran, and Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf, are those who deny some of what has been revealed to you. Say: "I have only been commanded to worship Allah alone and not to associate anything with Him. To His worship I call people, and to Him is my return and my final abode."

And just as We sent down the Scriptures to the prophets in their own tongues, We have sent down to you, O Messenger, the Qur'an in the language of the Arabs, so that you may judge by it. And if you were to follow the desires of the polytheists in worshipping other than Allah, after the truth that has come to you from Allah, then you would have no ally to support you and protect you from His punishment.

The commentary on Surah 13 (al-Ra'd), verse 38:

Meaning: The disbelievers said, "What is wrong with you, O Messenger, that you marry women?" So We sent messengers before you, from among mankind, and We gave them wives and offspring. And when they said, "If he were a messenger, he would bring what we asked for of miracles," it is not within the power of any messenger to bring a miracle that his people desire, except by the permission of Allah. For every term decreed by Allah there is a Book, and a fixed time which Allah has written with Him, which neither advances nor delays.

Allah erases whatever He wills of the rulings and other matters, and affirms whatever He wills of them, for a wisdom that He knows. With Him is the source of the Book, which is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), in which all the states of creation until the Day of Resurrection have been recorded.

And if We show you (O Messenger) some of the punishment with which We threatened your enemies, of disgrace and humiliation in this world, then that is what is hastened for them. And if We take you (in death) before you see that, then your duty is only to convey the message, and upon Us is the reckoning and the recompense.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 13, verse 41:

Have these disbelievers not seen that We come to the land, reducing it from its outlying parts? That refers to the Muslims' conquest of the lands of the polytheists and their annexation to the lands of the Muslims. Allah, glorified is He, judges; there is none who can repel or nullify His judgment and decree. He is swift in reckoning. So let them not hasten the punishment, for everything that is coming is near.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 13, verse 42:

Those before them had certainly plotted against their messengers, just as these people have plotted against you. So to Allah belongs all plotting. He nullifies their plotting and turns it back upon them with failure and regret. He, glory be to Him, knows what every soul earns of good or evil, and it will be recompensed for it. The disbelievers will come to know, when they stand before their Lord, for whom the praiseworthy outcome will be after this worldly life. Indeed, it belongs to the followers of the messengers. In this is a threat and a warning to the disbelievers.

Those who disbelieve say to the Prophet of Allah, "O Muhammad, you have not been sent by Allah." Say to them: "Allah is sufficient as a witness, testifying to my truthfulness and your falsehood, and sufficient is the testimony of those who have knowledge of the Book, from among the Jews and Christians, who have believed in my message and in what I have brought from Allah, and who follow the truth. He has declared that testimony and did not conceal it."
